name: ASE K19A advanced packaging plant (with WUS), Nanzih, Kaohsiung
aliases: ASE and WUS advanced AI packaging facility

parties.name: Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Inc.
parties.note: Named in the companies' releases as ASE (日月光半導體), a member of ASE Technology Holding; the build-and-share contract was disclosed for this subsidiary.

parties.name: ASE Technology Holding
parties.note: Parent group; it disclosed the build-and-share contract on behalf of its subsidiary.

parties.name: WUS Printed Circuit (楠梓電子)
parties.note: Printed circuit board maker that co-develops the building with ASE under a joint build-and-share contract, with the building value to be allocated about 97.26% to ASE and 2.74% to WUS; the sources do not say what each side contributes, and no separate venture company is reported.

summary: A new ASE advanced packaging building, K19A, in the Nanzih Technology Industrial Park, Kaohsiung, developed with printed circuit board maker WUS under a joint build-and-share contract disclosed in March 2026. The companies presented the plan in May 2026, when a groundbreaking ceremony was held. The eight-storey building, with two basement levels and about 113,400 square metres of floor space, is to make FOCoS fan-out and flip chip BGA packages for AI, cloud and autonomous driving chips and will get the park's first 161 kV substation. Total investment is reported at NT$35.2 billion and operations are planned to start in September 2029.

metrics.note: Total investment reported by United Daily News, citing ASE; the companies' releases give no amount.
The English release rounds this to more than 2,000.

milestones.note: ASE disclosed the joint build-and-share contract with WUS for the K19A building, to be signed on 31 March 2026.

notes: The companies' releases do not use the K19A name or mention a ceremony; the building number and the groundbreaking come from news reports. Total floor area (113,402 square metres in the Chinese release) is a building figure rather than cleanroom or site area, so it is not recorded as a metric.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Identified the project as ASE's K19A building, changed the status from announced to under construction after news reports of a groundbreaking on 8 May 2026, added the NT$35.2 billion investment, site area, March 2026 build-and-share contract and planned September 2029 opening, corrected the jobs figure to about 2,050 and added the Chinese release and two news sources. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): set the operator to Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Inc., the company named in the releases and the contract disclosure, with ASE Technology Holding as parent owner; kept WUS as joint-venture partner and noted that the sources do not say what each side contributes; labelled the TechNews copy as a Central News Agency report read via TechNews; and linked the record to the two other ASE projects in the Nanzih Technology Industrial Park.
